text: If you have a friend who is in a bad relationship, should you say something or should you keep it to yourself? One of my viewers has this type of problem, so here's what the subscriber wrote. Hello, good morning, afternoon and evening. I would like to ask for advice about my female friend. She told me that her old ex-boyfriend treated her miserably. Even after they broke up, she still sees his posts online, either by stalking his profile or by staying connected with him in some way. She recently found out that her ex now has a new girlfriend and he treats this new girl much better than he treated her. Meanwhile, my friend also has a new boyfriend, someone who can give her everything she wants and treats her well. However, she still misses her old ex and wants to receive the same treatment he is now giving to his new girlfriend. I think this is a really bad sign, but I don't know how to properly give advice or explain it to her. I hope you can read this and give advice not only to her, but also to others who are in a similar situation. I love your videos and thank you very much. So here was my answer. Hi, thank you for your question. I'm not sure if you're a guy or a girl, but there are several things I want to address here. First, why do you even need to give advice or explain anything to her? In general, I would advise you to refrain from giving advice to your friends unless they specifically ask for it, because chances are she won't listen to you in the first place. And even if she does and then something goes wrong, you can easily end up being blamed for the outcome. So live your life, take care of yourself and stay happy. Second, I already made a video about a similar situation where a girl keeps blaming her exes for being toxic, abusive, etc. Please watch it. It can give you some food for thought. Basically, I say that in many cases, those girls themselves can be problematic and it's better to stay away from relationships with them. You need to understand this. The choices of a partner tell you a lot about a person. They chose those guys and they stayed with them. So if they now find a guy who treats them well, they still might miss the emotional rollercoaster. And because of that, the chances of their new relationship being healthy long term are pretty small. That said, from the limited information you provided, it seems like your friend is problematic, complaining about her ex while stalking him and staying connected, being in a new relationship but missing the old one. Honestly, I wouldn't even be surprised if her ex is treating his new girlfriend the same way he treated her. But because your friend is problematic herself, she experienced it as abuse. And now from the third-person perspective, she suddenly thinks he's treating her well. If there's anyone who needs advice here, it is actually the new boyfriend of your friend because the way it looks, she is not treating him that well at all. She's missing her ex and still emotionally connected. If I would give advice to that guy, I would suggest to stay away from her. Overall, it's also questionable why you are even friends with her. I doubt she's a good friend to you either. And especially if you're a man, being real friends with girls is generally not the best idea. Acquaintances? Okay. Sharing common interests? Fine. But better spend your time working on yourself and becoming a better version of you instead of trying to help other people.
